$comment: Cover sheet for an IMPORTED project, plus the inventory it cannot supply for itself. A first-party catalog declares its components with @CatalogComponent / @CatalogVariant beside the @Preview functions and omits `groups` entirely; a project imported without its maintainers' involvement has no such annotations and never will, so the inventory is written down HERE. That is the one thing an import costs, and it is the honest place for it: this is our description of somebody else's code, and it stays in our repository.
title: BikeShare

components.caption: The upstream project's own preview: one station row built from a literal Station, with the free-bikes-to-empty-slots split drawn as an availability bar.
Grand Canal Dock — 17 free of 20 slots (0.85), which lands in the bar's top colour band.
Smithfield North — every slot holding a bike (1.00), the widest the bar gets.
Docklands Empty — no bikes left (0.00), the low band and the zero-width end of the bar. The state a rider most needs to read at a glance.
Three stations as the list stacks them. This is the only preview that shows the middle band: Portobello Harbour sits at 0.40, between the 0.20 and 0.50 thresholds.
One network row — dublinbikes, with the city and country line the network list is built from.
Three networks across Dublin, Paris and Barcelona, so an accented, longer name (Vélib' Métropole) sits beside short ones.
One country row from the country picker.
The three sample countries as the picker stacks them.
The Material 3 colour roles as labelled swatches — primary, secondary, tertiary, surface and error, each with its `on` colour used for the label.
The theme's type scale, one specimen line per style, each set in a station name.
